scheme_name: HIMAYAT- Deen Dayal Upadhyaya-Grameen Kaushalya Yojana
description:
HIMAYAT is a skill development initiative launched by the Government of India under the Deen Dayal Upadhyaya-Grameen Kaushalya Yojana. 

The scheme was launched in 2016. 

It aims to enhance the employability of rural youth. 

The primary objective is to provide skill training to 1 million rural youth by 2022. 

The program focuses on youth aged between 15 and 35 years. 

It targets those who are from Below Poverty Line families. 

The scheme aims to bridge the skill gap in rural areas. 

It also seeks to promote entrepreneurship among rural youth. 

The HIMAYAT scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development. 

The National Rural Livelihoods Mission oversees the execution of the program. 

The scheme provides financial assistance for skill training. 

It offers a training cost of up to INR 15,000 per candidate. 

The training duration ranges from 3 to 12 months. 

The training is provided through various training partners. 

These partners include NGOs and private sector organizations. 

The training is aligned with the National Skill Qualification Framework. 

Participants receive a monthly stipend of INR 2,000 during the training period. 

Upon successful completion of the training, candidates receive a certificate. 

The certification is recognized by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship. 

The scheme also provides placement support to trained candidates. 

The placement support includes job fairs and linkages with employers. 

The scheme emphasizes skill development in sectors like agriculture, construction, and hospitality. 

It also focuses on sectors like retail, healthcare, and information technology. 

The HIMAYAT scheme has a special focus on women and marginalized communities. 

At least 30% of the beneficiaries are expected to be women. 

The scheme encourages self-employment through entrepreneurship development programs. 

The application process for HIMAYAT is straightforward. 

Candidates must approach the nearest training center or training partner. 

They need to fill out an application form provided by the training partner. 

Required documents include proof of age, income certificate, and educational qualifications. 

Candidates must also provide a passport-sized photograph. 

Once the application is submitted, the training partner verifies the details. 

Selected candidates are then informed about the training schedule. 

The training centers are located in various rural areas across India. 

The scheme has been implemented in multiple states including Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, and Uttarakhand. 

The program has seen participation from over 200,000 youth since its inception. 

As of 2023, the scheme has successfully trained over 100,000 candidates. 

The placement rate for trained candidates stands at approximately 60%. 

The HIMAYAT scheme also collaborates with local industries for job placements. 

This collaboration ensures that the training provided is relevant to the local job market. 

The scheme has received positive feedback from beneficiaries. 

Many beneficiaries have reported improved job opportunities. 

The government aims to expand the program to reach more rural youth. 

The HIMAYAT scheme is part of a larger effort to enhance rural livelihoods. 

It aligns with the government's vision of a skilled India. 

The scheme also contributes to the overall economic development of rural areas. 

The financial allocation for the scheme has been increasing each year. 

In the financial year 2021-22, the government allocated INR 500 crore for skill development initiatives. 

The HIMAYAT scheme plays a crucial role in this allocation. 

The scheme also focuses on creating awareness about skill development. 

Awareness campaigns are conducted in rural areas to attract youth. 

These campaigns highlight the importance of skill training for employment. 

The scheme encourages partnerships with local self-governments. 

This collaboration helps in identifying potential candidates for training. 

The HIMAYAT scheme also emphasizes the importance of soft skills. 

Soft skills training is integrated into the skill development programs. 

This training includes communication skills, teamwork, and problem-solving. 

The scheme has provisions for monitoring and evaluation. 

Regular assessments are conducted to measure the impact of the training. 

Feedback from beneficiaries is collected to improve the training programs. 

The HIMAYAT scheme has been recognized for its innovative approach. 

It has been featured in various national and international forums. 

The success stories of beneficiaries are often shared to inspire others. 

The scheme has the potential to transform the lives of rural youth. 

By providing them with the necessary skills, it empowers them to secure better livelihoods. 

The HIMAYAT scheme is a significant step towards achieving sustainable rural development. 

It addresses the challenges of unemployment and underemployment in rural areas. 

The government continues to monitor the progress of the scheme closely. 

Future expansions of the scheme are planned based on the success of current initiatives. 

The HIMAYAT scheme stands as a testament to the government's commitment to rural development. 

It aims to create a skilled workforce that can contribute to the nation's economy. 

Through this initiative, the government envisions a prosperous and self-reliant rural India.
